newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 81 -1 on last week
Cow (90 CL) 78 n/c
Cow (85 CL) 75 n/c
Shank (90 CL) 76 -1
Trimmings (85 CL) 73 -1
Chucks (85 CL) 76 -1
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 147 +1 on last week
Chilled grassfed loin:striploin 230 n/c
cube roll 290 +10
tender loin 585 +60
Frozen Chuck/blade 94 n/c

AMLC COMMENTARY: Prices for imported grining beef declined slightly this week in the U.S.
The market was reported as quiet, with relatively steady prices due to the Christmas holiday season.
Offerings were limited and several market participants said they would not do much until the holidays conclude.
Prices for U.S. domestic lean grinding beef moved higher on Wednesday, the result of very cold weather in some northern parts of the U.S. and concerns about shortened working weeks over the holiday.
Although Australian lean grinding beef prices ended down for the week ending December 18, most falls were limited to one U.S. cent a pound.
Australian exporters reported that trade with Japan in the lead up to Christmas has picked up both for chilled and grassfed beef.
Export prices for grassfed fullsets increased slightly this week to 147 USc/pound C&F, with Japanese buyers securing orders for January delivery.

Lean beef prices are expected to move much higher in the U.S. over the next week, as many barns will be closed and accumulating cows for processing will become difficult, even without weather problems.
Bull meat sustained the most activity this week, as both east and west coast prices declined.
Offerings from New Zealand have slowed and Australian activity remains very limited.
Australian cuts have seen very little interest and prices are reported as nominal.
Grassfed loin cuts have also been in demand, with tenderloin in short supply, trading around 580-590 US cents/pound, up 60 US cents/pound on last week.
The chilled shortfed fullset export price also has remained quite firm, with supplies of grainfed cattle relatively tight.
Shortfed fullsets are currently trading around 215 US cents/pound.
With the arrival of a couple of vessels this week, the supply of chilled Australian beef on the wholesale market increased.
The rise in supply has dampened wholesale prices slightly, though most cuts are still trading well.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
